# `js/file-header`

**A file starts with the project's header**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `@codelaw/rules-js` (npm) · `codelaw-rules-js` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX |
| **Turned on by** | no preset — name it in `[rules]` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | `headerFormat`, `isRegularExpression` |
| **Fix** | `suggest` — `codelaw fix --unsafe` applies it; review the diff, it can change behaviour (a file that has a different header needs it replaced, not added to; the reviewer decides) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.2 |
| **Ported from** | `eslint-plugin-sonarjs/file-header`, `tslint/file-header` |

## What it checks

A file must start with `headerFormat`, after a `#!` line if it has one: the text as written (`// Copyright Acme`, a `/* … */` block), or, with `isRegularExpression`, a regular expression the start of the file must match. A file that does not is reported on its first line, with a suggestion to put the header first (a regular expression has no text to insert, so its finding has none). An empty file is not reported. eslint-plugin-sonarjs 4.2.2's `file-header` (S1451), behaviour only (LGPL-3.0, L2), and TSLint's `file-header`, whose successor in any tool nobody found. A header regular expression that does not compile is reported once, on the first node.

With no `headerFormat` set the rule is silent: it reports nothing, not even that the option is missing, and the engine does not run it on a single node. It is in no preset; a project switches it on by setting the option under `[rules]` (or in a `[scope.<name>]` for some files).

In `codelaw.toml`, under `[rules]`: `"js/file-header" = { severity = "warn", options = { headerFormat = "// Copyright Acme\n" } }`.

**Why:** A licence or copyright notice has to be at the top of every file; the rule is the check that none was forgotten.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
npm install --save-dev @codelaw/rules-js
pip install codelaw-rules-js
```

**No preset turns it on.** Load its pack through any preset (`codelaw:js/recommended` here), then name the rule in `[rules]`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:js/recommended"]

[rules]
"js/file-header" = "error"
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"js/file-header" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `headerFormat` | `string` | `""` | the text every file starts with, or a regular expression when `isRegularExpression` is true |
| `isRegularExpression` | `boolean` | `false` | read `headerFormat` as a regular expression the start of the file must match |

**Every option at its default** — a starting point to copy:

```toml
[rules."js/file-header"]
severity = "error"

[rules."js/file-header".options]
headerFormat = ""
isRegularExpression = false
```

**The same, inline, with example values:**

```toml
[rules]
"js/file-header" = { severity = "error", options = { headerFormat = "// Copyright Acme\n", isRegularExpression = true } }
```

- **A table without `severity`** changes only the options: the severity stays what a preset or an earlier layer set, and a rule that is off stays off.
- **A list option replaces its default** — copy the default entries you want to keep.
- **An unknown option or a value of the wrong type** stops the run with exit 2 and names the nearest option.

#### `headerFormat`

*string* · default `""`

the text every file starts with, or a regular expression when `isRegularExpression` is true

```toml
[rules."js/file-header".options]
headerFormat = "// Copyright Acme\n"
```

#### `isRegularExpression`

*boolean* · default `false`

read `headerFormat` as a regular expression the start of the file must match

```toml
[rules."js/file-header".options]
isRegularExpression = true
```

### Options in action

Each case below is one of the rule's tests (`packs/js/rules/js/file-header.cases.md`): the options, the input, and what codelaw reports.

#### a missing header

```toml
[rules."js/file-header".options]
headerFormat = "// Copyright Acme\n"
```

```js
run();
```

**Reports** at `1:1`.

#### the header is there

```toml
[rules."js/file-header".options]
headerFormat = "// Copyright Acme\n"
```

```js
// Copyright Acme
run();
```

**Reports nothing.**

#### a shebang comes first

```toml
[rules."js/file-header".options]
headerFormat = "// Copyright Acme"
```

```js
#!/usr/bin/env node
// Copyright Acme
run();
```

**Reports nothing.**

#### a regular expression

```toml
[rules."js/file-header".options]
headerFormat = "// Copyright \\\\d{4} Acme"
isRegularExpression = true
```

```js
// Copyright 2026 Acme
run();
```

**Reports nothing.**

#### a regular expression that does not match

```toml
[rules."js/file-header".options]
headerFormat = "// Copyright \\\\d{4} Acme"
isRegularExpression = true
```

```js
// Copyright Acme
run();
```

**Reports** at `1:1`.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — the `tests` scope `codelaw:js/recommended` ships (`**/*.test.*`, `**/*.spec.*`); naming it extends it, so its files stay:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/file-header" = { options = { headerFormat = "// Copyright Acme\n" } } }
```

Or switch it off there:

```toml
[scope.tests]
rules = { "js/file-header" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"js/file-header" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"js/file-header" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"js/file-header" = { severity = "warn", options = { headerFormat = "// Copyright Acme\n" } }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "js/file-header": {"severity": "warn", "options": {"headerFormat": "// Copyright Acme\n"}}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **JavaScript:** `// codelaw-ignore js/file-header: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `// codelaw-ignore js/file-header expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule js/file-header --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain js/file-header       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule js/file-header  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>  # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

### JavaScript
